html:
Mary Prince was born into slavery in Bermuda around 1788. Her book, The History of Mary Prince, published in London in 1831, was the first account of the life of a Black woman to appear in Britain.

She was sold several times and worked in Bermuda, in the salt ponds of the Turks Islands and in Antigua. Brought to London by her owners in 1828, she left them and found help from the Anti-Slavery Society.

Her plain telling of beatings and family separations shocked readers. It went through three printings in its first year and fed the campaign that led to the Slavery Abolition Act of 1833, which ended slavery across the British Empire.
